minutes.headline: Zoning Board granted a special permit to tear down and rebuild a non-conforming house at 90 Hemlock Drive.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard one petition: the Hudsons' request under the non-conforming structures section to remove and reconstruct a single-family home at 90 Hemlock Drive. The chair read the application, the engineer's letter and comments from town boards. The board asked about footprint, bedrooms, septic and grading, then voted by roll call to grant the permit and adjourned.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals voted by roll call to grant a special permit to tear down and rebuild a non-conforming house at 90 Hemlock Drive.
The permit carries conditions: compliance with all local, state and federal requirements, periodic review, and recording at the Registry of Deeds before it takes effect.
The board heard the application, an engineer's letter and town board comments, then asked about footprint, bedrooms, septic and grading.
No members of the public commented, and the meeting adjourned after the single petition.

why_it_matters: Rebuilding a non-conforming house under a special permit lets the owners replace it without bringing the lot fully into line with current zoning, so decisions like this shape what gets built in a neighborhood.
The questions on septic and grading are the points that bear most on neighbors and on the town's health and drainage rules, and the permit's periodic review is the mechanism for checking them.
